cards.subject: The outer city
lines: The aqir built this. The faction that took the south-west ransacked it, renamed itself qiraji, and slept in it for thousands of years while its numbers grew.
Then the gates closed for a thousand years and nobody swept up. It is not ruined by war so much as by neglect — an insect city that stopped being maintained.

cards.subject: You can look up
lines: Molten Core, Blackwing Lair, Onyxia, Naxxramas, the Temple through the other door — every one of them is an interior.
This one is broken stonework on sand, under the Silithus sky.
You can ride a mount inside it.

cards.subject: Twenty, not forty
cards.tag: The size that let guilds exist
lines: Vanilla raiding was forty people. This and Zul'Gurub were the exceptions.
They are the reason a guild could raid at all without a forty-person roster.
Retail later cut the Ruins to ten. In here it is twenty.

cards.subject: The first boss sees stealth
lines: An unusually wide aggro radius, and he spots rogues, so nobody scouts ahead of this one.
His sand trap silences casters and takes three quarters of your chance to hit.
You stand in a hole in the floor and wait it out.

cards.subject: Five NPCs fight beside you
lines: When Kurinnaxx dies a human general and four night elf sentinels spawn and hold the line with the raid through seven waves.
They can be kept alive or lost.
Almost nothing else in vanilla stands next to you and dies with you.

cards.subject: He is quoting Schwarzenegger
lines: Andorov opens the wave event with "Remember, Rajaxx, when I said I'd kill you last? I lied..." — verbatim Commando.
Mid-fight: "If it bleeds, we can kill it." Verbatim Predator.
He is a human, leading four night elves.

cards.subject: He is shouting at somebody who is not there
lines: Between waves: "Staghelm will whimper and beg for his life, just as his whelp of a son did!" and "Fandral! Your time has come!"
He killed Valstann Staghelm himself, in the war.
Fandral never comes. He is taunting an absent enemy across a millennium.

cards.subject: If he lives, he sells you things
lines: Andorov still standing at the end briefly opens a vendor window.
Then he goes: "My work here is done. I'll be sure to let Mar'alith and the others at Cenarion Hold know that you helped me out..."
A boss fight whose reward includes a merchant you had to keep alive.

cards.subject: A statue that has to be starved
lines: He drains the raid's mana and stores it, and when he is full he throws the whole lot back as one explosion.
Casters drain him back down to keep him empty.
He also turns to stone periodically — immune, inert — and spits out mana fiends while he waits. He can be walked straight past.

cards.subject: You kill him with his own eggs
lines: He cannot be taunted. He fixates on one player and gets faster the longer he chases them.
The raid blows up eggs while he is standing over them, which hurts him badly and resets his speed.
The entire fight is done by the floor.

cards.subject: The altar is not scenery
lines: A random raider is pinned to the stone sacrifice platform, and larvae start crawling toward the body.
They have to be killed before they arrive.
Go and stand on it before you pull.

cards.subject: He is the one who threw the sword
lines: The obsidian blade that brought a bronze dragon out of the sky was thrown by this Anubisath, and it very nearly killed him doing it.
C'Thun put him back together and bound his essence into the crystals scattered across his own floor.
The room is his leash, and you drag him around it.

cards.subject: What you carry out is a shopping list
lines: Scarabs and idols off the trash, ceremonial rings off the bosses, and all of it goes back to Cenarion Hold to be traded.
Your standing with the Circle decides what you are allowed to buy.
The bronze dragonflight's side of it is through the other door.
